PARKING AND TRAFFIC COMMISSION
August 2019 Meeting Minutes

Commissioners
Michael Benbow  Chairperson
Charles Braggs  District 1
Leonel Garcia  District 2
Brett C.S. Roberts  District 3
Barbara Brooks  District 4

Staff Members
Peter Puglese  TE, PE, City Traffic Engineer
Raquel Méndez  Associate Engineer (Transportation)
Mario Inga  Parking & Enterprise Service Manager
Diana Maximo  Serco Manager
Lieutenant Cardell Hurt  Traffic Unit Commander

1. Roll Call
   A meeting of the Parking and Traffic Commission was held at City of Inglewood’s Community Room located on
  the 1st Floor on August 28, 2019, at 19:03.
   All Commissioners and City Staff attended with the exception of Commissioner Brett C.S. Roberts

2. Approval of Minutes for August 28, 2019
   Motion to accept the meeting minutes was made by Commissioner Leonel Garcia.
   Seconded by Commissioner Charles Braggs
   3-2 approved Meeting Minutes

3. Public Comments (not listed on the agenda)
  Some of the issues that residents consulted the Commission were the following.
   Homeless and Parking Shortage at Grace Avenue and Hillcrest Boulevard
  o Residents had been experiencing a shortage of parking due to constant events at Blessed Family Covenant
  Church. Residents mentioned that they have communicated with Code Enforcement in this situation but only
  helped temporarily. Lieutenant Cardell Hurt provided contact information for residents to direct this message
  and find a solution.
  o Homelessness and unwanted waste or garbage left near the residential area on Grace Avenue and Hillcrest
  Boulevard. Public Works along with the Police Department agreed to investigate the situation and answer this
  request.

    A parking permit petition was presented to the Commission due to the shortage of parking on Park Way between
  67th and 68th Street. The Public Works (PW) Department took the form and informed residents of the citywide
  residential permitted parking study that is currently under way. PW will determine if the street will be included in
  the citywide study or will be studied independently.

    Stop Sign was requested on 64th Street and Chester Avenue. Public Works provided an intake form to the resident
  to fill out so the matter can be investigated.

    Vehicles sold and parked on Crenshaw Boulevard and Hawthorne Boulevard, which eliminates parking to residents.
  The Commission informed the resident that this is code enforcement to handle. Lieutenant Cardell Hurt also
  provided information on who to call on these matters.

    Speeding on Manchester Boulevard and Briarwood Lane/Crenshaw Drive is a constant battle. Lieutenant Cardell
  Hurt provided solutions to monitor this issue with the support of Public Works.

4. Unfinished Business
   PW Department explained the block party process and expressed the concern of not receiving barriers and barricades
  after a block party. The PW Department proposed to charge the applicant with a refundable deposit fee when
  applying for a block party. The Parking and Traffic Commission recommended that the PW Department proceeds
  with an investigation into how this $25.00 refundable deposit fee can be implemented into the current block party
  program procedures.
  a. Public Works reached out to the City Finance Department for help on how a refundable fee can be charged
  during the application process. The Finance Department recommended to Public Works that the fee should be
  set at an amount to recover 100% of the cost.
  b. PW Department informed the commissioners of the Finance Department’s recommendation. This issue will be
  presented again to the Commission when more information is obtained.

5. New Business
   None

6. Public Hearing
   None

7. Resolution
   None

   None

   None

   None

11. Commissioner Initiatives
   None

12. Adjournment
   The meeting was adjourned at 20:13

13. Announcements
   Next scheduled meeting date is September 25, 2019

1. Roll Call
   A meeting of the Parking and Traffic Commission was held at City of Inglewood’s Community Room located on
  the 1st Floor on July 26, 2019, at 19:07.
   All Commissioners and City Staff were present with the exception of Commissioner Barbara Brooks and Diana
  Maximo.

2. Approval of Minutes for July 24, 2019
   Motion to accept the meeting minutes was made by Commissioner Leonel Garcia
   Seconded by Commissioner Braggs
   4-1 approved Meeting Minutes

3. Public Comments (not listed on the agenda)
   Resident provided comments on speeding and shortage of parking on 110th West Street between Prairie Avenue and
  Doty Avenue. Resident then provided a speed hump and parking permit petition application. Lieutenant Cardell
  Hurt also provided information on who to call on these matters.

4. Unfinished Business
  a) None

5. New Business
   The Public Works (PW) Department explained the block party process and expressed the concern of not receiving
  barriers and barricades after a block party. The PW Department proposed to charge the applicant with a refundable
  deposit fee when applying for a block party. The Parking and Traffic Commission recommended that the PW
  Department proceeds with an investigation into how this refundable deposit fee can be implemented into the current
  block party program procedures.
   Public Works Department looked into the intersection of Fairview Blvd & La Tijera Boulevard. City Staff explained
  that the intersection was recently modified to improve visibility and reduce speeds.

6. Public Hearing
   None

   None
